solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Rod, having wasted time, also stops for snack

indicators.note: the word for 'also' stops up the gap, plugging the shortened rod
wasting something means losing it, so the time letter goes from the rod

parts.note: a switch is a thin rod or cane used for beating
and means also, in addition

explanation.surface: Someone wields a rod, wastes time, and pauses for a bite to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having wasted' and 'stops' both read as part of the story of an idle afternoon; one removes the time letter, the other plugs the gap.
explanation.definitionFit: Two slices of bread around a filling is the classic light meal or snack.

clue.text: Independent politician described by broadcaster as mean …

indicators.note: described means drawn round, so the broadcaster encircles the politician

parts.note: Sky is a British television broadcaster
MP, Member of Parliament, is a politician

explanation.surface: A broadcaster portrays an independent politician as stingy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'described by' puts IMP inside SKY.
explanation.definitionFit: Skimpy means meagre or stingy, the same sense as mean in giving too little.

clue.text: … to arrest a small child

parts.note: to nip is an informal word for to catch or arrest
per means a, as in so much a head

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: a mean politician tries to arrest a little child.
explanation.definitionFit: Nipper is informal British for a young child or kid.

clue.text: Church ceremony, baptism, requires two days for tourist on vacation

indicators.note: for means in place of, so two days stand in for the letters taken from the tourist

parts.note: a wetting is a baptism, as in wetting a baby's head

indicators.note: vacated means emptied, leaving only the outside letters of tourist

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for day, so two days give DD

explanation.surface: A holidaying tourist's christening needs a couple of days.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on vacation' empties tourist to TT, and DD takes their place in WETTING.
explanation.definitionFit: A marriage service is a ceremony usually held in church.

clue.text: Pore over periods announced to obtain reduced-price tickets

parts.note: to con is to study or pore over

indicators.note: announced means spoken, so the word for periods is heard rather than written

parts.note: sessions are periods of time

explanation.surface: Someone studies timetables announced for discount tickets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'announced' turns SESSIONS into the like-sounding CESSIONS.
explanation.definitionFit: Concessions are discounts for groups such as students or pensioners, so reduced-price tickets.

clue.text: Mention being upset by letter that brings everything up

indicators.note: by here means placed beside, so the reversed word follows the letter

parts.note: em is the name of the letter M

indicators.note: in a down-or-across clue being upset turns the word over, so it reads backwards

parts.note: to cite is to mention

explanation.surface: Raising a subject upsets someone over a letter that brings everything out into the open.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being upset' does the reversing; the letter is M spelt out as its name, the printer's measure.
explanation.definitionFit: An emetic is a substance taken to induce vomiting, so it makes the stomach's contents come up.

clue.text: Bovine epidemic in Northern Ireland area half-ignored, strange to recall

indicators.note: recall means calling back, so the whole string is read backwards
half of the word area is ignored, leaving the front half

parts.note: rum is British slang for strange or odd

explanation.surface: A cattle disease outbreak in a region of Northern Ireland, half forgotten, is odd to remember.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to recall' reverses NIARRUM.
explanation.definitionFit: Murrain is an old term for infectious disease of cattle, such as foot-and-mouth.

clue.text: Picked up dessert with herb topping, one due to go off later?

definitions.text: one due to go off later?

indicators.note: something picked up is caught by ear, signalling a sound-alike

parts.note: a bombe is a moulded ice-cream dessert; thyme, the herb, goes on top in a down clue

explanation.surface: Someone takes an ice-cream pudding decorated with herbs that will go off later.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go off' suggests food spoiling; it means exploding.
explanation.definitionFit: A bomb with a timer is designed to explode at a set moment in the future.

clue.text: General acceptance of groom keeping bride's last name undisclosed essentially

indicators.note: keeping means holding within, so the groom word holds the letters

parts.note: to curry a horse is to groom it

indicators.note: last points to the final letter of bride
essentially means at its essence or core, the centre letter of undisclosed

explanation.surface: A groom keeps his bride's surname a secret.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keeping' puts E, N and C inside CURRY.
explanation.definitionFit: Currency means widespread acceptance or prevalence, as when an idea gains currency.

clue.text: Disrespectful and unwise to snub Republican

indicators.note: to snub is to ignore or cut someone, so the Republican letter is cut out

parts.note: imprudent means unwise or rash

explanation.surface: Snubbing a Republican is described as both rude and foolish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to snub' removes R from IMPRUDENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Impudent describes cheeky, insolent behaviour lacking respect.

clue.text: Introductory textbook, gloss over it perhaps?

definitions.meaning: a basic school book teaching the elements of a subject
the preparatory coat of paint over which a gloss topcoat is applied

explanation.walkthrough: 'gloss over' suggests skating past something; here gloss is literally paint going on top.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses share the idea of preparation: a basic reader for beginners, and an undercoat preparing a surface.

clue.text: Cooked crepes, one is filling for definite

indicators.note: the numeral sits inside the shuffled pancakes like a filling
cooked suggests ingredients worked over into a new form, signalling an anagram

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Pancakes are made, and one has a filling, certainly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cooked' rearranges CREPES into PRECSE, and 'is filling' puts I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Precise means exact or definite, with no vagueness.

clue.text: Little Abraham suffered cut after pruning prickly shrub

parts.note: Bram is a short form of Abraham, as in Bram Stoker

indicators.note: pruning trims off the end, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: someone who suffered a cut bled

explanation.surface: Young Abraham got cut while pruning a thorny bush.
explanation.walkthrough: Bram Stoker, author of Dracula, supplies the short form of Abraham; 'after pruning' trims the final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The blackberry bush is a thorny, sprawling plant, the standard prickly shrub of hedgerows.

clue.text: Buys a larger, boiled type of sweet

indicators.note: boiling churns things up, signalling a rearrangement of the letters

explanation.surface: Someone buys a larger boiled sweet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boiled' rearranges BUYSALARGER.
explanation.definitionFit: Barley sugar is a hard amber boiled sweet, an example of a type of confectionery.

clue.text: Gut originally enormous, suggestive of eating good food

indicators.note: originally points to the start of the word gut, its opening letter

parts.note: astronomic means enormous, of vast size

explanation.surface: An enormous gut hints at someone who eats well.
explanation.definitionFit: Gastronomy is the art of good eating, so this adjective relates to fine dining.

clue.text: Bet Russia surprisingly losing international is hard to understand

indicators.note: surprisingly suggests something unexpected, signalling letters in a new order
losing means dropping, so the international letter is removed

explanation.surface: A wager on Russia unexpectedly losing an international match is baffling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing' drops I from BETRUSSIA, and 'surprisingly' rearranges BETRUSSA.
explanation.definitionFit: Abstruse means obscure or difficult to comprehend.

clue.text: Vermilion-coloured crab wandering around island, attracting news article

indicators.note: around says the shuffled crab letters surround the rest
wandering suggests straying from position, signalling an anagram
attracting means drawing others to it, so the following letters join on

parts.note: N stands for new, so two Ns give news
A is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A crab roams round an island and draws a newspaper story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wandering' rearranges CRAB to CBAR, and 'around' puts INNA inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Cinnabar is a red mercury mineral, and its name serves as a shade of bright scarlet.

clue.text: Transport as far as Paddington, say, provides exercise

parts.note: to bring is to carry or transport
to means as far as, up to
Paddington is the famous fictional bear from Peru

explanation.surface: Taking someone to Paddington station gives them a workout.
explanation.walkthrough: Paddington looks like the London station; it is the children's-book bear.
explanation.definitionFit: To exercise influence or pressure is to apply it, the meaning of this idiom.

clue.text: Justification for area of land that encircles building

definitions.meaning: a reason or basis for an action

definitions.text: area of land that encircles building
definitions.meaning: the gardens and land around a large house

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses share a word: a basis or reason, and the estate land surrounding a mansion.

clue.text: Greatly admired wine always gets consumed

indicators.note: consumed here means swallowed whole, so one word is taken inside the other

parts.note: red is wine of that colour
ever means always

explanation.surface: A much-loved wine is always drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets consumed' tells you one word swallows the other; the wine is simply red.
explanation.definitionFit: Revered means deeply respected or venerated.

clue.text: Occasionally call out that fellow as cover

indicators.note: occasionally means now and then, so only every other letter is used

parts.note: he is the pronoun for that fellow

explanation.surface: Now and then shout to that man to act as cover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Occasionally' takes CLOT from the odd letters of call out.
explanation.definitionFit: To clothe is to dress or cover with garments.

clue.text: Agree to how to restyle one's hair?

definitions.meaning: split as an instruction: give it a perm, putting waves or curls in

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits into PERM + IT, an instruction to curl one's hair.
explanation.definitionFit: To give permission is to allow or sanction, so it means agreeing to something.

clue.text: Weak sun out, moving over rear of house

indicators.note: moving signals the letters shifting position into a new order
the rear of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A feeble sun has come out, shifting across the back of the house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving' rearranges SUNOUT with E, the last letter of house.
explanation.definitionFit: Tenuous means thin, slight or flimsy, as with a weak argument.

clue.text: City content to cancel live show, on reflection

indicators.note: on reflection says the hidden letters are read backwards
content here is the noun: what the following words contain

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone is happy to scrap a live performance, having thought it over.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'City content' as the definition, but 'content' is the hiding signal; the city alone defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Seville is a major city in Andalusia, southern Spain.

clue.text: Discovered how Sikh men traditionally appear elegant

indicators.note: dis-covered means the cover is removed, stripping both outer letters

parts.note: Sikh men traditionally wear a turban, so they appear turbaned

explanation.surface: Traditionally dressed Sikh men are found to look stylish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Discovered' removes the outer letters T and D from TURBANED.
explanation.definitionFit: Urbane means smoothly courteous and sophisticated, polished in manner.

clue.text: Plant boss sacking staff leads to acrimonious trade union meeting

indicators.note: sacking means dismissing, so the staff word is thrown out

parts.note: a manager is a boss
to man is to staff, as in manning a desk

indicators.note: the leads of the following words are their initial letters

explanation.surface: A boss firing workers sparks a bitter union meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sacking' removes MAN from MANAGER, leaving AGER; 'leads' gives ATUM.
explanation.definitionFit: Ageratum is a genus of low garden flowers with fluffy blue heads, an example of a plant.

clue.text: Kew Gardens at intervals shut off southern exit

indicators.note: the southern letter shuts off the sequence, closing it at the end
at intervals signals taking letters spaced regularly, every second one

explanation.surface: Kew Gardens periodically closes its southern exit.
explanation.walkthrough: Kew Gardens is a botanic garden in London. 'at intervals' takes its even letters, EGRES.
explanation.definitionFit: Egress is a formal word for a way out or the act of leaving.

clue.text: Rise in subsidy about to stop suddenly

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the subsidy word goes round the other

parts.note: a grant is a subsidy
an engine that stops suddenly is said to die

explanation.surface: A rise in subsidy is about to come to an abrupt halt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about to' looks like a phrase meaning soon; 'about' is the containment signal and 'to stop suddenly' is the inner word.
explanation.definitionFit: A gradient is a slope, so an upward one is a rise in the road.
